title: William Grey smiles with his photograph's own teeth
items: William Grey of 2010 Prairie (1904) now rests with his mouth shut, as his side photographs and his portrait show it, and breaks into the front photograph's grin when you stand in front of him or he greets you.
Behind his lips are the photograph's own teeth, and the smile was fitted to the photograph: the opening between his lips matches it to a third of a millimetre on average.
When he talks his jaw moves with it, the groundwork for giving him a voice later.
Sarah Grey's photographs show her mouth shut, so she is unchanged.
Still short of the photographs: the nose and moustache seen from the front, his temple hair, and the front of his beard seen from the side.
